newsitem.title: USA: Weekend rain favored northwest U.S. Midwest - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Weekend rain favored northwest U.S. Midwest - WSC.

text.p: The northwestern U.S. Midwest received 0.3 to 1.5 inches of rain over the weekend, while eastern areas received light scattered showers that produced less than 0.5 inch of moisture, said Weather Services Corp.
"There wasn't a lot of (rain) activity east of the Mississippi," said Joel Burgio, WSC meteorologist.
Rain amounts of 0.25 to 1.00 inch were forecast for southeastern Illinois on Monday and lesser amounts with 30 percent coverage were forecast for the rest of the state.
"The dry area should be missed again," Burgio said of central Illinois.
WSC data showed that 30-day rainfall near Peoria, Ill., was 12 percent of normal at 0.50 inch.

The current storm system should move east bringing 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain from southeast Illinois to Ohio by Tuesday Burgio said. After that, the Midwest will turn hot through Thursday with high temperatures from the high 80s degrees Fahrenheit to the mid-90s.
Rain forecast for central Illinois early this week should fall during the hottest part of the day, which may lessen the benefit to the crops.
"Temperatures in the 80s and 90s pull a lot of moisture out of the ground," he said.
More showers were likely Thursday in the northwest Midwest and Friday in east and southwest Midwest.
"We don't expect to see a lot of activity with this, possibly 0.2 to 0.6 inch and around 50 percent coverage," he said.
